item.title: Iran’s Basij chief praises 'resistance cinema', saying that 'change has begun' in US, Israel
item.description:
Iran’s Basij chief praises 'resistance cinema', saying that 'change has begun' in US, Israel

Iran’s Basij commander Hossein Taeb has said that the US and Israel are seeing change amid their ongoing attempts at transforming the Middle East's landscape.

"Today, we say that change has begun in America and Israel, and we will soon see it across different areas," he said during the closing ceremony of the 19th International Resistance Film Festival in Tehran.

His highlighted the use of media and film as a way of "disrupting America’s media monopoly", describing it as "resistance cinema".

"The staging of this festival under such circumstances signifies that - much like a combatant who never abandons their launchers during military defence - an artist engaged in the 'perceptual battlefield' does not desert their post, even under the shadow of war, economic siege, or any other threat," he said.

"Through their portrayal of the Resistance, they inflict a new defeat upon the enemy."

Referencing US-Israeli attacks on Gaza, Lebanon, Iraq and Syria, Taeb said: "All these crimes took place; children were killed, and the oppressed peoples of the region suffered. Yet, the true losers in this conflict were the United States and Israel."

Israeli forces demolish five West Bank buildings and displace over 100 Palestinians
item.description:
Israeli forces demolish five West Bank buildings and displace over 100 Palestinians

Israeli forces demolished five Palestinian residential buildings in the occupied West Bank on Thursday without warning, displacing more than 100 people.

Troops raided the town of Biddu, northwest of Jerusalem, in the early morning, forcing residents of 12 apartments out before demolishing them.

Residents said soldiers fired stun grenades and tear gas at homeowners, preventing them from retrieving their belongings before the demolitions began.

The Jerusalem Governorate office has recorded a significant increase in demolitions and land-clearing operations in Jerusalem and its surrounding areas this year.

During the first nine months of 2026, it documented 427 operations, including 66 cases of forced self-demolition, in which Palestinians were compelled to tear down their own homes; 294 demolitions carried out using Israeli machinery; and 32 land-levelling operations.

In October alone, the office recorded a further 44 demolition and land-levelling operations, bringing the total number documented between January and the end of October to 471.

item.title: Israeli president Herzog deliberates after Eisenkot receives majority Knesset backing to become prime minister
item.description:
Israeli president Herzog deliberates after Eisenkot receives majority Knesset backing to become prime minister

Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot has received the backing of a majority of Knesset members to be prime minister, possibly granting him the mandate to attempt to form the next government.

Eisenkot received 67 recommendations compared with 46 for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The Yashar party urged Israeli president Isaac Herzog on Thursday to hand Eisenkot the mandate to form the next government "as soon as possible", adding that its the largest number of recommendations given to a candidate for forming a government since 2015.

"Benjamin Netanyahu is a caretaker prime minister leading a minority of just 46 seats," the party said. "He has no mandate, no majority and no public trust."

While Herzog expressed that the result was "clear", he indicated that he would hold further talks with party leaders to clarify the situation before assigning the mandate to form a government on Sunday.

item.title: Israel issues tenders for 91 settlement units in occupied West Bank, revises E1 tender schedule
item.description: Israeli authorities issued two new tenders for the construction of 91 settlement units in the northern occupied West Bank and revised the timetable for another settlement tender east of Jerusalem, a Palestinian organization said Thursday, Anadolu reports. The Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission said in a statement that the two tenders cover land in the illegal Oranit settlement, built on land in the Qalqilya governorate. The 91 units are divided among seven compounds, with the first tender covering four compounds for 86 multi-story housing units. The second tender covers three compounds for five low-rise settlement units. Bidding is scheduled to open Nov. 16 and close Dec. 29. item.title: Egypt, Saudi Arabia urge diplomacy to prevent renewed military confrontations in region
item.description: Egypt and Saudi Arabia on Thursday called for prioritizing dialogue and giving diplomacy more time to prevent renewed military confrontations in the region and their consequences, Anadolu reports. The appeal came during a phone call between Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty and his Saudi counterpart Prince Faisal bin Farhan, according to a statement by the Egyptian Foreign Ministry. Ministry spokesman Nader Zaki said the two ministers discussed joint efforts to restore calm and prevent regional escalation in coordination with regional and international partners, including the US and Qatar. The ministers stressed the need to prioritize wisdom and dialogue, allow more time for diplomatic and political efforts, and encourage the parties concerned to engage in negotiations and demonstrate the necessary flexibility. item.title: Gaza civil defense warns heavy rains, strong winds threaten nearly 950,000 displaced Palestinians
item.description: Gaza’s Civil Defense warned Thursday that heavy rainfall and strong winds expected Friday could endanger displaced Palestinians living in tents and temporary shelters, as well as families staying in damaged buildings at risk of collapse, Anadolu reports. The warning comes as nearly 950,000 displaced Palestinians live in areas exposed to moderate or high flood risks, according to UN figures. In a statement, the Palestinian Civil Defense Directorate urged residents to take preventive measures to avoid potential dangers associated with the weather system expected to affect the enclave Friday. item.title: Abdul El-Sayed backs Trump’s call to cut Israel aid, says he is willing to work with president
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed, the first Muslim American elected to the US Senate, voiced support Thursday for President Donald Trump’s remarks about cutting aid to Israel, saying Washington should stop financing a military accused of committing atrocities with American weapons, Anadolu reports. El-Sayed told MS NOW that he agreed with Trump’s position and was willing to work with the president to end US military assistance to Israel. “I agree with him on that. I don’t think we should be continuing to subsidize a foreign military that had done the worst things with our money. I agree. I would love to work with him on doing that,” he said.
